extra.message: The createTable mapper statement uses MyBatis string substitution ${sql}, interpolating the SQL text directly into the statement. GenController.createTableSave passes a user-supplied 'sql' request parameter that is only lightly filtered (SqlUtil.filterKeyword) and re-serialized from the Druid AST before reaching this sink, so an attacker able to invoke /tool/gen/createTable (admin role) can influence the executed DDL. String substitution (${}) is the classic SQL-injection sink; use #{param} or a strict allow-list/validation of the whole statement.

selectUserList appends ${params.dataScope} to the SQL via string substitution. The 'params' map is bound from the request (BaseEntity.params) and is only overwritten by DataScopeAspect when the service method carries @DataScope; any code path reaching a dataScope mapper without that aspect would allow an authenticated user to inject arbitrary SQL through params[dataScope]. Use parameterized fragments or construct the clause server-side only.

selectAllocatedList concatenates ${params.dataScope} directly into the query. This is an unparameterized SQL fragment sourced from the request-bound params map, an injection sink if the @DataScope clearing aspect is not applied.
selectUnallocatedList concatenates ${params.dataScope} directly into the query, an unparameterized SQL fragment from the request-bound params map.
selectRoleList concatenates ${params.dataScope} into the SQL statement via string substitution, a SQL-injection sink if the params map value is attacker controlled.
selectDeptList concatenates ${params.dataScope} into the SQL statement via string substitution, a SQL-injection sink if the params map value is attacker controlled.

The JWT signing secret is hardcoded to the trivially guessable value 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'. TokenService signs (HS512) and verifies tokens with this value, so a leaked/guessed secret allows token forgery. Secrets must be supplied from an external secret store, not committed to the repository.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Database credentials are hardcoded in the committed configuration (username root, password 'password' at lines 10-11). Hardcoded production database credentials can be extracted from source control and lead to full compromise of the data tier.

The Druid monitoring console credentials are hardcoded (login-username: ruoyi, login-password: 123456) and the console is enabled with an empty IP allow-list, exposing an administrative console with well-known default credentials.

The Spring Security filter chain permits anonymous access to /druid/**, /swagger-ui/** and /v3/api-docs/**. The Druid stat view servlet exposes SQL, session and datasource internals; combined with the default console credentials this is a serious unauthenticated information-disclosure / administrative exposure.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Hardcoded user credentials are embedded in source ('admin'/'admin123', 'ry'/'admin123'). These demo accounts and passwords ship in the application.

GET /test/user/list serializes the full UserEntity objects, including the password field, to any authenticated caller. Passwords should never be returned in API responses (CWE-200 sensitive information exposure).

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The XSS filter is explicitly configured to exclude /system/notice from sanitization. Notice title/content is stored via SysNoticeController.add/edit and later rendered, so attacker-supplied HTML/JavaScript is persisted without escaping, enabling stored XSS.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: handleExcludeURL returns true (i.e. skips XSS sanitization) for all GET and DELETE requests. Any input carried in GET query parameters therefore bypasses the XSS filter entirely, which is a filter bypass that undermines the application's XSS mitigation.

extra.message: GET /system/config/configKey/{configKey} has no @PreAuthorize annotation, unlike the other endpoints in this controller. Any authenticated user (regardless of system:config:query permission) can read arbitrary configuration values by key, potentially disclosing sensitive system settings.

GET /system/menu/roleMenuTreeselect/{roleId} has no @PreAuthorize and no data-scope check on roleId. Any authenticated user can retrieve the menu/permission assignment of any role, an object-reference authorization flaw (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: GET /system/notice/{noticeId} has no @PreAuthorize annotation, so any authenticated user can read arbitrary notices by ID even without the system:notice:query/list permission.

authRole(userId) fetches the target user and its roles without calling userService.checkUserDataScope(userId). A user holding only system:user:query can therefore read user/role data for users outside their assigned data scope (IDOR / broken access control).

extra.message: cancelAuthUser / cancelAuthUserAll operate on an arbitrary roleId and userIds without calling roleService.checkRoleDataScope(roleId) (unlike selectAuthUserAll at line 238). A user with system:role:edit can revoke role assignments for roles outside their data scope.

extra.message: Generic RuntimeException and Exception handlers return the raw exception message (e.getMessage()) to the client (lines 101 and 112). Internal exception details, SQL errors and class names can leak implementation information useful to attackers.

extra.message: The CORS configuration allows any origin pattern ('*'), any header and any method for every path (/**). A wildcard cross-origin policy exposes authenticated API responses to arbitrary web origins.

extra.message: ImageUtils.readFile opens a URLConnection to any attacker-influenced string beginning with 'http' with no host allow-list (and, for non-http values, reads an arbitrary local path derived from the value). This is a Server-Side Request Forgery / arbitrary-file-read primitive; it is reachable through ExcelUtil image handling at ExcelUtil.java:1164 when entity fields contain URLs.

Druid's SQL wall filter is configured with multi-statement-allow: true. Allowing multi-statement SQL amplifies the impact of any SQL injection by permitting stacked/arbitrary statements to be executed.

PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH is set to 5. Registration and login accept passwords as short as 5 characters (SysLoginService.loginPreCheck, SysRegisterService.register), which permits weak, easily brute-forced credentials.
